newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil asks coffee exporters for no new June sales.
newsitem.headline: Brazil asks coffee exporters for no new June sales.

text.p: Brazil's government has asked coffee exporters to make no further sales for June shipment after evaluating current exports in light of a limit agreed with other producing countries, an official said.

The government also asked exporters to roll over as much as possible exports at the end of June until the beginning of July, said Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry.
"There was a consensus. We asked the exporters to transfer as much as possible exports from the end of June to July and not to make any further sales for June shipment," Assis said.
Assis was speaking after a meeting with officials from Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Federation (Febec).
Febec president Oswaldo Aranha said that exporters understood the government's position and would cooperate as much as possible as long as it would not be to the detriment of consumers.
"Our position is to cooperate with the government fully without harming our clients," Aranha said.

Assis, however, was confident that exporters would comply with the government request. "We will not make any more June sales," he said. He said there was no question however of the government actually closing June export registrations.
Assis declined to give any estimates of January to June exports.
Under an agreement with members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), Brazil should not have shipped more than six million bags between January and June this year.
But according to export statistics, shipments to the end of May had already exceeded this level.
Aranha said that May shipment figures to be finalized shortly are expected to be between 1.2 and 1.3 million bags. June exports, he anticipated would be between 600,000 and 900,000 bags.
Under the ACPC plan, Brazil was to export a total of 15 million bags between July 1996 and June 1997. It shipped slightly over its nine million bag quota in the July to December period.
Now, however, Aranha estimated the country would ship around 1.2 million bags over its 1996/97 allowance.
Aranha also estimated that possibly more than 200,000 bags which would have been shipped in June will now be shipped in July as a result of the government's request.

Despite the higher than expected export performance, Assis said that the government still estimated the 1996/97 coffee crop at between 25 and 26 million bags. Its forecast for the 1997/98 harvest also remained unchanged at 22 million bags.
Assis said that the excess shipments made by Brazil were no cause for concern and attributed the higher sales to a series of factors including high prices and tight international supply.
"The volume that Brazil is selling above its ACPC limit is positive as it is bringing reassurance to consumers," he said.

Febec is traditionally Brazil's main exporting body. Another entity -- the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Association (Abecafe) -- was also expected to cooperate with the government request with regard to June sales, both officials said.

Although Abecafe did not officially participate in the meeting, one of its key members had taken part in the discussion in his capacity as a representative of another coffee organization, they added. ((--Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom +55 21 507 4151))
